title: The Discovery of Oz, the Terrible, part 3
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: “Yes,” she answered, “I melted her with a bucket of water.”
“Dear me,” said the Voice, “how sudden! Well, come to me tomorrow, for I must have time to think it over.”
“You’ve had plenty of time already,” said the Tin Woodman angrily.
“We shan’t wait a day longer,” said the Scarecrow.
“You must keep your promises to us!” exclaimed Dorothy.

The Lion thought it might be as well to frighten the Wizard, so he gave a large, loud roar, which was so fierce and dreadful that Toto jumped away from him in alarm and tipped over the screen that stood in a corner. As it fell with a crash they looked that way, and the next moment all of them were filled with wonder. For they saw, standing in just the spot the screen had hidden, a little old man, with a bald head and a wrinkled face, who seemed to be as much surprised as they were. The Tin Woodman, raising his axe, rushed toward the little man and cried out, “Who are you?”
“I am Oz, the Great and Terrible,” said the little man, in a trembling voice. “But don’t strike me—please don’t—and I’ll do anything you want me to.”
Our friends looked at him in surprise and dismay.
“I thought Oz was a great Head,” said Dorothy.
“And I thought Oz was a lovely Lady,” said the Scarecrow.
“And I thought Oz was a terrible Beast,” said the Tin Woodman.
“And I thought Oz was a Ball of Fire,” exclaimed the Lion.
“No, you are all wrong,” said the little man meekly. “I have been making believe.”
“Making believe!” cried Dorothy. “Are you not a Great Wizard?”
“Hush, my dear,” he said. “Don’t speak so loud, or you will be overheard—and I should be ruined. I’m supposed to be a Great Wizard.”
“Not a bit of it, my dear; I’m just a common man.”

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what tipped over the screen?
options: Toto, jumping away from the Lion's roar
The Tin Woodman's swinging axe
A gust of wind from the open door
The Scarecrow stumbling against it

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what was standing where the screen had been?
options: A little old man with a bald head
A great painted Head on a wire
A ball of cotton soaked in oil
Nothing at all

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Tin Woodman do?
options: Rushed at the little man with his axe raised
Ran straight out of the Throne Room
Laughed until his jaws began to rust
Knelt down before the little old man

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the little man beg them not to do?
options: Strike him
Tell the people
Leave the city
Call the Monkeys

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the little man call himself at the end?
options: Just a common man
A very great Wizard
A servant of the real Oz
The King of the Winkies

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did the Lion roar just then?
options: He thought it might frighten the Wizard into keeping his word
He had been startled by the Voice from the dome
He was angry at Toto for knocking the screen
He wanted to prove he had found his courage

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what do the four different answers show?
options: Each of them had met Oz in a different shape
None of them had really seen Oz at all
They could not agree on what they saw
The Wizard had lied to only one of them

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the little man ask Dorothy to speak quietly?
options: If he were overheard he would be ruined
The Voice would drown out her words
He was hard of hearing in that room
The soldier was listening at the door

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does making believe mean?
options: Pretending to be something he is not
Persuading people by argument
Believing something without proof
Making promises he cannot keep

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: An accident with a screen exposes the Wizard as an ordinary man
The Wizard appears in yet another terrible shape
The Tin Woodman destroys the Wizard with his axe
The travellers agree to wait one more day

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did Dorothy say she melted the Witch?
options: With a bucket of water
With the silver shoes
With the Golden Cap
With the Woodman's axe

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Voice ask for when it heard the news?
options: Time to think it over until tomorrow
Proof that the Witch was dead
The Golden Cap as payment
The travellers to leave the city

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who said they would not wait a day longer?
options: The Scarecrow
The Tin Woodman
Dorothy
The Lion

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how did the little man react to being found?
options: He trembled and offered to do anything they wanted
He ordered them out of the Throne Room
He vanished behind the screen again
He laughed at their astonishment

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what was the Tin Woodman's tone when he objected to waiting?
options: Angry
Amused
Frightened
Sorrowful

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does dismay mean?
options: Dismayed shock at what they found
Delight at a happy surprise
Boredom at a long wait
Anger at being kept waiting

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: A roar, a fallen screen, and the end of a long pretence
A bargain struck between the travellers and the Wizard
A fight in which the Wizard is driven from his throne
